John Masefield | John Edward Masefield, OM ( ; 1 June 1878 – 12 May 1967) English poet and writer, was Poet Laureate of the United Kingdom from 1930.  Among his best known works are the children's novels "The Midnight Folk" and "The Box of Delights", and the poems "The Everlasting Mercy" and "Sea-Fever".
The Foundation Pit | The Foundation Pit (Russian: Котлован, "kotlovan") is a gloomy symbolic and semi-satirical novel by Andrei Platonov.  The plot of the novel concerns a group of workers living in the early Soviet Union. The workers dig each day but slowly cease to understand the meaning of their work.  The enormous foundation pit sucks out all of their physical and mental energy.
The Box of Delights | The Box of Delights is a children's fantasy novel by John Masefield.  It is a sequel to "The Midnight Folk", and was first published in 1935.

The award resumed in 1967 following the visit of Queen Elizabeth to Germany and the last prize was awarded in 2006.

The novel is set in 1911, sometime after Don Manuel, the benevolent dictator in Sard Harker, has died.  It is an adventure story about the taking of a ship called 'the Gry'.  It additionally features the only known map (or, rather, map illustration) of the City of Santa Barbara, and an Appendix setting out fictional historical background to Santa Barbara.
John Masefield High School | John Masefield High School is a secondary school with academy status located in Ledbury, Herefordshire.

The Glasgow canons elected John de Lindesay to succeed him without knowing of the papal reservation, while the pope himself provided the Englishman John de Egglescliffe to the see.
